pages.textMedium:
It was Nana's birthday. There were balloons. There was a cake. There was a party hat that kept slipping down over one ear.

And there was one big problem.

Nuni had forgotten to get him a present.
pages.textLong:
It was Nana's birthday. There were balloons. There was a cake. There was a party hat that kept slipping down over one ear.

And there was one big problem.

Nuni had forgotten to get him a present.

pages.textMedium:
Now, if you know one thing about birthdays, it's this: the birthday rabbit wants a present he really, really loves.

And can you guess what Nana loves most in the whole world?

Correct. Carrots.
pages.textLong:
Now, if you know one thing about birthdays, it's this: the birthday rabbit wants a present he really, really loves.

And can you guess what Nana loves most in the whole world?

Correct. Carrots.

pages.textMedium:
So Nuni looked for a carrot. He looked in the fridge. He looked in the garden. He looked under the sofa, where he found a sock, a marble and an old cracker.

But no carrot. Not one.
pages.textLong:
So Nuni looked for a carrot. He looked in the fridge. He looked in the garden. He looked under the sofa, where he found a sock, a marble and an old cracker.

But no carrot. Not one.

pages.textMedium:
He looked in the hall cupboard. He found a trumpet, one roller skate and a spider who told him to shut the door.

He looked inside the piano. PLONK. He even looked in his own ears.

"Nuni?" called Nana. "What are you doing in there?"

"Tuning the piano!"

No carrot. Not half a carrot.
pages.textLong:
He looked in the hall cupboard. He found a trumpet, one roller skate and a spider who told him to shut the door.

He looked in the bathtub. He looked inside the piano. PLONK.

He even looked in his own ears.

No carrot. Not half a carrot.
pages.scene: The burrow hallway, a little away from the party. Nuni stands inside an open upright piano with the lid up, lifting one of his own long ears and peering into it with one eye, very serious. On the floor behind him lie a trumpet and a single roller skate. Lively detail: in the open hall cupboard a small cross spider is pulling the door shut with one leg. A balloon has drifted in from the party room.

pages.textLong:
He ran outside. Once, a carrot as big as a bus had lain right here. Now there was only a carrot-shaped dent in the grass. That was a hundred breakfasts ago.

"NUNI!" called Nana from inside. "Are you coming?"

"Just tying my shoe!"

Rabbits do not wear shoes.
pages.scene: Outside the round burrow door in the green hill, the same place where the roasted giant carrot landed in The Biggest Carrot in the World. Nuni stands in the middle of a huge carrot-shaped dent pressed into the grass, looking down at it glumly, paws hanging. Nana, in his party hat, leans out of the round window calling and waving. Nuni looks back over his shoulder with a too-innocent smile. Lively detail: the little snail from the first story sits in the dent, and a balloon is tied to the door knob.

pages.textMedium:
He opened the kitchen cupboard. A potato. Too lumpy. An onion. He imagined Nana unwrapping it. He imagined Nana crying.

Right at the back he found one pea. One.

"Happy birthday, Nana. Here is your pea."

No.
pages.textLong:
He opened the kitchen cupboard. A potato. Too lumpy. An onion. He imagined Nana unwrapping it. He imagined Nana crying.

Right at the back he found one pea. One.

"Happy birthday, Nana. Here is your pea."

No.
pages.scene: The burrow kitchen. Nuni stands at the counter holding one single green pea up between two fingers, right in front of his nose, looking at it with a flat, unimpressed face. On the counter lie a lumpy potato and an onion; the onion has made his eyes water, with one tear on his cheek. Behind him the wooden kitchen cupboard stands open. Lively detail: the small spider in the cupboard corner dabbing its eyes with a tiny handkerchief because of the onion.

pages.textMedium:
"Think, Nuni, think," said Nuni.

He opened the cupboard one last time. And there, all alone in the fruit bowl, lay a banana. Long. A bit pointy at the end.

Nuni looked at the banana. The banana looked back.
pages.textLong:
"Think, Nuni, think," said Nuni.

He opened the cupboard one last time. And there, all alone in the fruit bowl, lay a banana. Long. A bit pointy at the end.

Nuni looked at the banana. The banana looked back.

pages.textMedium:
"It's ALMOST a carrot," whispered Nuni. He fetched his paint box.

Small problem. The orange was all dried up.

So he tried red. It looked like a sausage. He tried green. It looked like a pickle. He tried purple with yellow spots.

Nobody knows what that looked like.
pages.textLong:
"It's ALMOST a carrot," whispered Nuni. He fetched his paint box.

Small problem. The orange was all dried up.

So he tried red. It looked like a sausage. He tried green. It looked like a pickle. He tried purple with yellow spots.

Nobody knows what that looked like.
pages.scene: Nuni at the wooden table with the open paint box, a jar of water and brushes. He holds up the banana, now painted purple with yellow spots, at arm's length and stares at it with one eyebrow up and his mouth pulled to one side, clearly doubtful. Smears of red and green paint on the table and on his paws show the earlier tries. Lively detail: the pink worm hanging from the ceiling covers its eyes with its tail.

pages.textLong:
Then he remembered. Red and yellow make orange! He mixed. He dipped his brush. He squeezed the banana tight —

FWIP!

Wet bananas are slippery. It shot out of his paw, bounced off the lamp and stuck to the ceiling.

"NUNI? What was that?"

"Just brushing my teeth!"
pages.scene: The same table. The wet, half-orange banana has shot out of Nuni's paw and is stuck flat to the earth ceiling, a dotted arc and an orange smudge on the swinging lamp showing how it got there. Nuni stands frozen with his brush in one paw and the other paw still squeezed shut around nothing, looking straight up, mouth a small round o. A big blob of freshly mixed orange sits in the lid of the paint box. Lively detail: the pink worm in the ceiling, right beside the banana, staring at it in shock with an orange splat on its head.

pages.textMedium:
Then he remembered. Red and yellow make orange! He mixed it up and painted that banana orange from top to bottom. He stuck a little bunch of parsley on the end.

Then he stood back. "Genius," said Nuni.
pages.textLong:
He got it down with a broom. He painted that banana orange from top to bottom. He stuck a little bunch of parsley on the end.

It was still a bit bent. "A bent carrot," said Nuni. "Very rare."

Then he stood back. "Genius."

pages.textMedium:
The paint had to dry. So Nuni went and played musical chairs. It was Nana, Nuni and the worm from the ceiling.

The worm won. Nobody knows how.

"Nuni," said Nana, "why is your nose orange?"

"Sunburn," said Nuni, and left the room very fast.
pages.textLong:
The paint had to dry. So Nuni went and played musical chairs. It was Nana, Nuni and the worm from the ceiling.

The worm won. Nobody knows how.

"Nuni," said Nana, "why is your nose orange?"

"Sunburn," said Nuni, and left the room very fast.
pages.scene: The party room with balloons, bunting and the cake on its little table. One chair stands in the middle of the green rug; the pink worm has let itself down from the ceiling and sits curled on the seat, smug. Nana, in his party hat, has stopped mid-dash and points a paw at Nuni's nose with a curious face. Nuni, with a clear orange smudge on his nose, grins much too widely and is already tiptoeing sideways toward the door. Lively detail: an old gramophone with a big horn that has just stopped playing.

pages.textLong:
Now for the hard part. His face.

Nuni stood at the mirror and practised. First face: too guilty. Second face: he looked like he needed the toilet. Third face: far too many teeth.

He tried a fourth. It had a lot of teeth as well.

It would have to do.
pages.scene: The hallway. Nuni stands in front of a round wall mirror pulling a huge, stiff grin with all his teeth showing, eyebrows up, trying to look innocent; the mirror shows the same ridiculous grin back. He still has the orange smudge on his nose. Behind him on the window sill the finished orange banana with its parsley top is drying. Lively detail: the small spider hanging beside the mirror on a thread, copying the grin.

pages.textMedium:
He put the carrot — okay, the banana — into a beautiful box. He tied it with a big red ribbon.

Then he carried it to Nana with his very best nothing-is-wrong face.

"Happy birthday, Nana!"
pages.textLong:
He put the carrot — okay, the banana — into a beautiful box. He tied it with a big red ribbon.

Then he carried it to Nana with his very best nothing-is-wrong face.

"Happy birthday, Nana!"

pages.textMedium:
Nana tore off the ribbon. He opened the box.

"A CARROT! The biggest one I ever got!"

He gave Nuni a hug. Nuni smiled a slightly wobbly smile.

Then Nana opened his mouth wide and took an enormous bite.
pages.textLong:
Nana tore off the ribbon. He opened the box.

"A CARROT! The biggest one I ever got!"

He gave Nuni a hug. Nuni smiled a slightly wobbly smile.

Then Nana opened his mouth wide and took an enormous bite.

pages.textMedium:
Squish.

Nana stopped chewing. His eyes went round. His ears stood straight up.

"Thith cawwot," he said with his mouth full, "tathtes FUNNY."

"BLEH! PFFFT! PTOOEY!" Orange bits flew all over the cake.
pages.textLong:

"Thith cawwot," he said with his mouth full, "tathtes FUNNY."

"BLEH! PFFFT! PTOOEY!" Orange bits flew all over the cake.

pages.textMedium:
It went very quiet. Even the worm held its breath.

Nana looked at the carrot. He sniffed it. He scratched it. Orange came off on his paw. Underneath, it was yellow.

"Nuni," said Nana slowly. "Why does my carrot have a peel?"
pages.textLong:
It went very quiet. Even the worm held its breath.

Nana looked at the carrot. He sniffed it. He scratched it. Orange came off on his paw. Underneath, it was yellow.

"Nuni," said Nana slowly. "Why does my carrot have a peel?"
pages.scene: Close on Nana in the party room, party hat crooked. He holds the bitten orange 'carrot' in one paw and with the other peels back one strip of orange-painted skin, showing bright yellow peel and pale banana underneath. One eyebrow is up, his mouth is a thin puzzled line, and the tips of his paw are orange. Behind him Nuni peeks out between his own ears with one eye. Lively detail: the pink worm in the ceiling frozen stiff, eyes huge. Orange spots on the cake.

pages.textMedium:
Nuni's ears drooped all the way to the floor. "I forgot your present," he said in a very small voice. "It's a banana. I painted it."

Nana stared at Nuni. Nana stared at the banana.

And then Nana started to laugh. He laughed until he fell off his chair.
pages.textLong:
Nuni's ears drooped all the way to the floor. "I forgot your present," he said in a very small voice. "It's a banana. I painted it."

Nana stared at Nuni. Nana stared at the banana.

And then Nana started to laugh. He laughed until he fell off his chair.

pages.textMedium:
When Nana could breathe again, he held out the banana. "Your turn."

"No thank you," said Nuni.

"Birthday rules."

So Nuni took one tiny bite. Paint. Peel. Parsley.

"BLEH! PFFFT! PTOOEY!"

Now they were even.
pages.textLong:

pages.scene: The party room, the chair still tipped over. Now it is Nuni who spits out orange bits in a comic spray, his ears shooting straight up, eyes round, tongue out, exactly as Nana did before. Nana sits on the rug holding the banana with its two bites, pointing at Nuni and howling with laughter, party hat on the floor. Lively detail: the pink worm in the ceiling holding a small leaf over its head like an umbrella against the spray.

pages.textLong:
Then Nana wanted a go with the paint box.

They painted the potato to look like a strawberry. They painted the onion to look like an apple. They painted the pea to look like a very small carrot, and gave it to the worm.

The worm said nothing. Worms never do.
pages.scene: Nana and Nuni side by side at the table with the paint box, both with orange smudges on their noses, both delighted. Nana proudly finishes a potato painted red with little seed dots like a strawberry; an onion painted as a red apple with a paper leaf stands beside it. Nuni holds up a tiny orange-painted pea on the tip of a brush toward the pink worm hanging down from the ceiling. Lively detail: the worm eyeing the pea-carrot with deep suspicion. Paint drips and paw prints all over the table.

pages.textMedium:
"A painted banana!" gasped Nana. "That's the funniest present I ever got!"

He put it on the shelf, right next to his best trophy.

Then they ate cake until they were full, and that night two rabbits fell asleep with orange paint on their noses. Because even the toughest rabbits in the world have to sleep sometime.
pages.textLong:
"A painted banana," sighed Nana. "That's the funniest present I ever got."

He put it on the shelf, right next to his best trophy.

Then they ate cake until they were full, and that night two rabbits fell asleep with orange paint on their noses. Because even the toughest rabbits in the world have to sleep sometime.
